note: The fill-rate bands F-004's tier resolver judges its startup measurement against, in pixels shaded per second. Spike gate A7.3's rule is do not invent a number, so this file states the provenance of EACH figure separately: one is measured, one is derived from that measurement, and one does not exist yet. A recorded-but-not-consulted number must not read as a trusted one. crates/ocelli-render/src/caps.rs carries FillRateBands::RECORDED, and the test the_recorded_bands_match_the_checked_in_file asserts the constant and this file are one number.

workload.description: A full-viewport triangle into an offscreen texture, a fixed ALU count per fragment, repeated a fixed number of passes, one submission, no readback. The warm-up run's figure is discarded. A figure taken with a different workload is a different measurement and does not belong in this file.

bands.hardware_floor_provenance: DERIVED from the single measured figure below, and not itself a measurement. It sits at roughly a quarter of that figure, chosen so that a rate clearly faster than any plausible software rasteriser is called Hardware and nothing else is. A genuine but much slower GPU therefore lands in Unknown rather than Hardware, and is then decided by its reported adapter type, which is the designed fall-through and not a failure. Erring high is the safe direction here: the defect deviation D-07 exists to prevent is a rasteriser being called hardware, never the reverse. The figure tightens when measurements from more machines exist.
bands.software_ceiling_provenance: NOT MEASURED, and therefore absent rather than guessed. No software-rasteriser figure can be taken on the machine this was recorded on. While it is null the benchmark NEVER returns Software: a low rate is Unknown, and the combination rule falls through to the adapter type and then the renderer string, which is exactly what the resolver already does for a benchmark that did not decide. Whether lavapipe even resolves as a fallback adapter under the pinned wgpu is itself unproven and is F-X002's acceptance criterion, per docs/spikes/A7-tier-c.md section A7.2.

measurements.note: Five runs across the release and dev profiles, all within 17 percent of each other. One machine and one adapter, so this is a data point rather than a distribution. Taken on a workstation that was not otherwise idle, so the low end of the range is the more trustworthy half.

tolerance_note: No tolerance, deliberately. ci/wasm-size-budget.json carries one because it re-takes a measurement and asks whether it moved. This file is not that: the bands are a decision boundary that a measurement is judged against, and a tolerance on a boundary would be a third band nobody specified.
